title: Choose the visual world for Zamani Grill & Market
question: The roll assigned the Levant Menu Card. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Your pinned constraint (light editorial, one accent, generous whitespace) binds every card.

options.label: Levant Menu Card
options.lineage: 1960s–70s Beirut hotel and Middle East Airlines dining menus: bilingual, coated card stock, one spot color
options.thesis: The menu is the page: every dish, price, and pickup time is set as typography on bright card stock, in English and Arabic at equal weight, and the photo is the garnish, never the ground.
options.viewport: A single wide card fills the first screen: bilingual wordmark top-left, language switcher and cart top-right, the first course (Shawarma, Mixed Grill, Family Dinners) already listed with live add buttons down the left two-thirds, one framed photo in the right third, and a cedar-green order rail pinned to the bottom edge on phones.
options.risk: Reads like a PDF menu if the add-to-cart controls are not visibly alive and the card has no pacing between courses.

raised.raise: Spot color commits at region scale: the order rail, the market band, and the catering close are solid cedar-green fields, never green sprinkled on white.
Every control is a distinct shape (round add, pill quantity, square remove) and state changes by fill, never by tint alone.
Size carries hierarchy: dish names at display scale, prices one step smaller in tabular figures, never a shouting price.
One vertical axis rules the card: a left ruler rail aligns every course heading, price column, and section break.
Text never sits on photography; every photo lives in its own framed plane.
Pickup times and price ladders render as stepped bands (ASAP · 20 min · 45 min · scheduled) instead of a dropdown.

options.label: Mezze Table From Above
options.lineage: the Lebanese family table photographed top-down: white enamelware, blue rims, dishes crowding a white cloth
options.thesis: The page is the spread: round dishes as the only image shape, arranged on a white cloth grid, so the first viewport is dinner already on the table.
options.viewport: Top-down circular plates of hummus, shawarma, and tabouli tile the first screen edge to edge with names and prices beside each; the order button sits in the one empty place setting.
options.risk: Also where most food-site runs land, and it depends on top-down photography the owner has not shot yet; stock plates will not match each other.

options.label: Risograph Web System
options.lineage: two or three fluorescent spot inks misregistered over warm paper
options.thesis: A flat spot-ink menu where green and gold overlap to a third color and every card shudders a hair off-register on hover.
options.viewport: Cut-paper shapes of dishes in two inks, the menu as blocky columns, misregister on hover.
options.case: Holds the paper-and-one-accent brief and brings total color commitment; loses on audience identification, since halal diners do not read Riso zines.
options.risk: Reads as an art-school zine, not a family restaurant, when the grain is heavy.

options.label: Memphis Showroom Morning
options.lineage: Memphis Milano terrazzo, squiggle laminate, candy geometry
options.thesis: Dishes as clashing toys on a speckled floor.
options.viewport: Menu sections as tilted furniture objects.
options.case: Loses both axes: a halal family grill is not a 1981 showroom, and clashing pattern hides prices.
options.kept: Distinct control shapes; state changes by fill.

options.label: Massin Stage Page
options.lineage: typeset theatre dialogue, size as volume
options.thesis: Dish names shout across the gutter in colliding sizes.
options.viewport: Courses as voices arguing across a spread.
options.case: Loses both: overlapping type fights the three-tap ordering job and the four RTL scripts.
options.kept: Size carries hierarchy, never color alone.
options.risk: Illegible in Urdu and Farsi at collision scale.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.lineage: technical dive down a volcanic wall, depth as axis
options.viewport: A vertical depth axis ruling every line.
options.case: Loses both: dark, cold, and unrelated to a grill; the pinned brief is light.
options.kept: One vertical axis rules every line of the card.

options.label: Multiplane Cel Dawn
options.lineage: hand-painted animation planes sliding at different speeds
options.thesis: Scroll sinks the camera through painted planes toward the grill.
options.viewport: Parallax forest planes with the restaurant as the lit cottage.
options.case: Loses both: heavy painted assets, parallax cost on phones in a parking lot, and no menu in the first viewport.
options.kept: Text always on the nearest plane; never over photography.
options.risk: Performance budget fails on cell data.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight Bay
options.lineage: amber safelight, timed baths, test strips
options.thesis: Dishes develop slowly under amber light.
options.viewport: Photos emerge in developer trays as you scroll.
options.case: Loses both: dark amber ground against the light pin, and slow reveals fight a hungry visitor.
options.kept: Stepped test-strip bands for pickup-time and price ladders.
options.risk: Slow by design; ordering is not.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The restaurant site every visitor expects: full-bleed food hero, Order Online button, three feature cards, review carousel, map footer, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Hero photo with headline and Order Online button, then About / Menu / Catering cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Zara's and Nadia's by design.
